page: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 architecture, powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, accompanied by 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance includes 640 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, one complimentary public IPv4 address, and operates without discrete GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations reveal pronounced single-thread capability alongside moderate multi-threaded throughput. In stress-ng single-core tests, the instance records a top-tier score of 3199.17, supported by a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2128.0 and top-tier text processing at 2837.0. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks align with mid-range expectations for a 4-vCPU platform, reflected in a stress-ng multi-core score of 12814.11 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6709.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth tests show 86.9 GB/sec for read operations and 60.95 GB/sec for write operations.

Performance constraints appear in heavy multi-threaded and specialized transactional benchmarks. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, PassMark database operations, and static web serving throughput fall into the lower 25th percentile. Furthermore, CPU-bound LLM prompt processing and generation benchmarks for 7B parameter models indicate low throughput. As a result, the server offers strong qualitative resource value for memory-intensive tasks and single-thread execution, but presents processing bottlenecks for parallelized batch processing or large-scale transactional workloads.

This hardware and performance profile aligns effectively with in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, lightweight application backends, single-threaded batch workers, and development databases requiring dedicated CPU stability and generous RAM capacity relative to vCPU count.
description: Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-640s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance equipped with 4 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs from 2 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at 2.0 GHz. It provides 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, combined with 640 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and no integrated GPU. In performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU execution and strong text processing, while multi-core metrics and large-block memory bandwidth perform within average bands. Lower relative scores are evident in static web serving, multi-threaded compression, and transactional database tasks. Delivering stable CPU dedication and high memory density per thread, this system is suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, microservices, and single-threaded background processing.
